idiom_name: HashMap<&str, fn(&[u8]) -> Result<T, E>> + rdkafka headers
implementation_notes: serde is content-based: tagged enums read their tag from the document (internally tagged with #[serde(tag = "type")], adjacently tagged, externally tagged, or untagged), and untagged enums are documented to try each variant in order and keep the first that deserialises - exactly the failure mode the property-based form avoids. The property channel comes from the client (rdkafka exposes BorrowedHeaders/OwnedHeaders on the message), and the registry is a hand-written HashMap<&str, fn>; read the header, resolve the parser, then decode the body exactly once.
pitfalls: An untagged serde enum compiles fine but silently picks the first variant that happens to deserialise, so a mislabelled header yields a wrong event instead of an error.
BorrowedHeaders borrows from the consumer's buffer and is only valid for the duration of the callback, so copy the token before any await or spawned task.
&str keys compare bytes exactly: a token with different casing or trailing whitespace misses the registry and must be rejected rather than silently trimmed.
